question:
Select the correct spelling to fill in the blank.

Wedding is an auspicious _______ for all.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. occasion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correctly spelt word is "occasion", meaning a particular time or event / a special or important event. (अवसर)

◦ Correct: Wedding is an auspicious occasion for all.

• Spelling key: OC + CA + SION (one "c" is doubled, single "s").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• The other options are misspelt — "occassion" (extra "s"), "occation" (wrong "t") and "ocassion" (single "c") are all wrong.

NOTE

• Remember: occasion has double "c" and single "s". Related word: "occasional" (happening from time to time), "occasionally".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Commence
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Start.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Commence" means to begin or start something. Its closest synonym is "Start". (आरंभ करना / शुरू करना)

◦ Example: The examination will commence/start at 10 a.m.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Subvert" (to undermine/overthrow), Option 2 "Exert" (to apply effort/force) and Option 4 "Escort" (to accompany) are unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Synonyms of commence: start, begin, initiate, launch, embark on. Antonyms: end, conclude, finish, terminate, cease.

question:
In the given sentence, one of the four underlined words is incorrectly spelt. Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word.

She dabbled in drawing and painting, but scalpture was her favourite medium.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. scalpture.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Scalpture" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "sculpture", meaning the art of making solid figures/objects by carving or modelling, or such a figure itself. (मूर्तिकला)

◦ Correct: ... but sculpture was her favourite medium.

• Spelling key: SCULP + TURE.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "drawing", "favourite" (British spelling) and "dabbled" are all correctly spelt.

• "Dabbled" means to take part in an activity in a casual, not serious way.

NOTE

• Related words: sculptor (a person who makes sculptures), sculpt (verb — to carve/shape). Do not confuse with "scalp" (skin of the head).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I couldn't believe how _______ the math problem was; it took me hours to solve it.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. complicated.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The clause "it took me hours to solve it" shows the problem was difficult. So the adjective "complicated" (difficult, involving many confusing parts) correctly fills the blank. (जटिल / पेचीदा)

◦ Correct: I couldn't believe how complicated the math problem was; it took me hours to solve it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "good" does not match the idea of difficulty.

• Options 3 "simply" and 4 "easily" are adverbs and also give the opposite (easy) meaning; the blank needs an adjective after "how" describing the noun "problem".

NOTE

• After "how + ___ + the noun was", an adjective (complicated), not an adverb (simply/easily), is required. Synonyms of complicated: complex, intricate, difficult.

question:
Read the following sentence and select its future tense form from the options given below:

Sarah and Fidha entered into an agreement to share the resources that are currently accessible.
option_1: Sarah and Fidha are entering into an agreement to share the resources that are currently accessible.
option_2: Sarah and Fidha will enter into an agreement to share the resources that are currently accessible.
option_3: Sarah and Fidha had entered into an agreement to share the resources that are currently accessible.
option_4: Sarah and Fidha were entered into an agreement to share the resources that are currently accessible.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Sarah and Fidha will enter into an agreement to share the resources that are currently accessible.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The simple future tense is formed with "will + base form (V1) of the verb". The base form of "entered" is "enter", so the future form is "will enter".

◦ Correct: Sarah and Fidha will enter into an agreement ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "are entering" is present continuous.

• Option 3 "had entered" is past perfect.

• Option 4 "were entered" is a wrong past passive form.

NOTE

• Simple future = will/shall + V1 (will enter, will go, will write). It expresses an action that will happen later.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.

When Mr. Bhanot was told a few years back that he needed to lose _____ or face health problems, he transformed his life with the _________ of a personal trainer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. weight; help.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The context is about health problems and a personal trainer, so one needs to lose "weight" and does so with the "help" of a personal trainer. (वज़न; मदद)

◦ Correct: ... he needed to lose weight or face health problems, he transformed his life with the help of a personal trainer.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "wait" is a homophone of "weight" but wrong in meaning here (to wait = to stay).

• Options 2 ("money; instructions") and 4 ("patience; guidance") do not fit the health/fitness context.

NOTE

• Homophones to distinguish: weight (heaviness) vs wait (to stay/pause). Both sound alike but differ in spelling and meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Confession is good for the soul ________________ after the soul has been claimed.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. even.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The adverb "even" is used to emphasise something surprising or extreme. Here it stresses that confession benefits the soul "even after the soul has been claimed" (i.e., in the most extreme case). (यहाँ तक कि)

◦ Correct: Confession is good for the soul even after the soul has been claimed.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "since" (because / from a time) and Option 2 "though" (although) change the logical relationship wrongly.

• Option 3 "still" would need a different sentence structure and does not give the emphatic sense required here.

NOTE

• "Even" adds emphasis: "even after", "even though", "even if". It highlights the unexpected or extreme nature of what follows.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

She was a ________, ________ __________astronaut.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. smart, tall, Indian.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When several adjectives come before a noun, they follow a fixed order of adjectives: Opinion → Size → Age → Shape → Colour → Origin → Material → Purpose.

◦ Here "smart" (opinion) comes first, "tall" (size) next, and "Indian" (origin) last, just before the noun "astronaut".

◦ Correct: She was a smart, tall, Indian astronaut.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• The other options place the adjectives in the wrong sequence (e.g., origin before size), which sounds unnatural in English.

NOTE

• A common mnemonic for adjective order is OSASCOMP (Opinion, Size, Age, Shape, Colour, Origin, Material, Purpose). Origin adjectives (Indian, French) always sit closest to the noun.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Callous
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Tender.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Callous" means insensitive, unfeeling and cruel; showing no concern for others. Its antonym is "Tender", meaning gentle, kind and caring. (कठोर / निर्दयी का विलोम — कोमल)

◦ Example: A callous remark hurt her, but his tender words comforted her.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Augment" (to increase), Option 2 "Desolate" (deserted/lonely — actually similar in gloom) and Option 4 "Beguile" (to charm or deceive) are not antonyms of callous.

NOTE

• Synonyms of callous: hard-hearted, insensitive, heartless, unfeeling. Antonyms: tender, kind, compassionate, sympathetic, caring.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym for the given word.

Species
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Type.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Species" means a class or kind/group of living things having common characteristics. Its closest synonym is "Type" (a kind, sort or category). (प्रजाति / प्रकार)

◦ Example: The zoo protects many species/types of endangered animals.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Whole" (entire/complete), Option 3 "Detail" (a small part/particular) and Option 4 "Multiply" (to increase in number) do not mean a kind or category.

NOTE

• Synonyms of species: type, kind, sort, class, category, variety. In biology, a species is a group of organisms that can interbreed.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Tranquil
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Unquiet.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Tranquil" means calm, peaceful and quiet. Its antonym is "Unquiet", meaning restless, disturbed and not calm. (शांत का विलोम — अशांत)

◦ Example: The lake was tranquil at dawn but grew unquiet during the storm.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "Composed" and 2 "Serene" are synonyms of tranquil (calm, peaceful).

• Option 3 "Shabby" (worn out/untidy) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of tranquil: calm, peaceful, serene, composed, placid, still. Antonyms: unquiet, restless, disturbed, agitated, turbulent.

question:
Identify the word with a spelling error in the following sentence. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.

In Shakespeare's play 'Hamlet', Hamlet's flaw is defined as procrustineition.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. procrastination.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The misspelt word "procrustineition" should be corrected to "procrastination", meaning the act of delaying or postponing something / putting off tasks. (टाल-मटोल / विलंब करना)

◦ Correct: ... Hamlet's flaw is defined as procrastination.

• Spelling key: PRO + CRAS + TI + NA + TION.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• The other options — "pracrostination", "procristineition" and "procrustination" — are all incorrect spellings.

NOTE

• Related words: procrastinate (verb — to delay), procrastinator (a person who delays). Famous saying: "Procrastination is the thief of time."

question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

Mary is the quieter student of the class.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. quietest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "of the class" implies a comparison among all the students of the class, which requires the superlative degree. The superlative of "quiet" is "quietest".

◦ Correct: Mary is the quietest student of the class.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "quieter" (comparative) is wrong because it compares only two things, whereas the whole class (a group) needs the superlative.

• "most quiet" and "more quiet" are wrong because a short adjective like "quiet" forms degrees with "-er/-est", not "more/most".

NOTE

• Degrees of "quiet": quiet – quieter (comparative, between two) – quietest (superlative, among many). Use "the + superlative" when comparing more than two.

question: Select the sentence with the most appropriate comparative degree.
option_1: She is the talent of all musicians in the orchestra.
option_2: She is the talentedest musician in the orchestra.
option_3: She is more talented musician in the orchestra.
option_4: She is the most talented musician in the orchestra.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. She is the most talented musician in the orchestra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Talented" is a long adjective, so its superlative is formed with "the most". Comparing one musician with all others "in the orchestra" needs the superlative degree — "the most talented".

◦ Correct: She is the most talented musician in the orchestra.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 uses the noun "talent" wrongly ("the talent of all musicians").

• Option 2 "talentedest" is a wrong form (long adjectives never take "-est").

• Option 3 "more talented" is a comparative but omits "the" and does not fit comparison with the whole group.

NOTE

• Long adjectives: comparative = "more + adjective" (more talented), superlative = "the most + adjective" (the most talented). Short adjectives take "-er/-est".

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains a grammatical error.

Ms. Malathi is old much to join a college now.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. old much.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct structure is "too + adjective + to + verb". So it should be "too old to join", not "old much to join". The segment "old much" is grammatically wrong.

◦ Correct: Ms. Malathi is too old to join a college now.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• The segments "Ms. Malathi is", "to join" and "a college now" are all correct.

NOTE

• "Too ... to" shows an excessive degree that prevents an action (too old to join = so old that she cannot join). "Much" is used with comparatives (much older), not directly before an adjective like this.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Let the cat out of the bag
option_1: To buy a cat and a bag
option_3: To not allow a cat into the bag
option_4: To release a cat out of a bag
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. To reveal a secret.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "let the cat out of the bag" means to reveal a secret carelessly or by mistake. (राज़ खोल देना)

◦ Example: She let the cat out of the bag and told everyone about the surprise party.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 3 and 4 give the literal (word-for-word) meaning, which is not what an idiom conveys. An idiom carries a figurative meaning.

NOTE

• Similar idioms about secrets: "spill the beans" (to reveal a secret), "give the game away", "blow the whistle" (to expose wrongdoing).

question:
Based on the situation in the sentence, choose the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

You cannot _________________ before replicating your successes and achievements multiple times; otherwise, people will deem your success a stroke of dumb luck.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. rest on your laurels.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "rest on your laurels" means to be so satisfied with past success that you stop making further effort. The sentence warns against relaxing after a single success. (पुरानी सफलताओं पर संतुष्ट होकर बैठ जाना)

◦ Correct: You cannot rest on your laurels before replicating your successes ... multiple times.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "play devil's advocate" (to argue the opposite side for the sake of debate), Option 2 "sit on the fence" (to remain undecided) and Option 3 "cut to the chase" (to come to the point) do not fit the context.

NOTE

• "Laurels" refers to the laurel wreath awarded to winners in ancient times, symbolising honour/achievement. "Rest on one's laurels" = to become complacent after success.

question:
Select the correct indefinite article to fill in the blank.

My neighbour is ______ passionate photographer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. a.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The indefinite article "a" is used before words beginning with a consonant sound. "Passionate" begins with the consonant sound /p/, so "a passionate photographer" is correct.

◦ Correct: My neighbour is a passionate photographer.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "an" is used before a vowel sound (an apple, an hour), which does not apply here.

• Option 4 "the" is a definite article (a specific one), not suitable for introducing a general description.

• Option 1 "one" is a number, not an article.

NOTE

• Rule of articles: "a" before a consonant sound (a boy, a university /yu/), "an" before a vowel sound (an egg, an honest man /o/). It depends on sound, not spelling.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the bracketed word in the sentence given below.

Surrounded by lush greenery, the house stood _____________ (submissively) atop a hill.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Proudly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Submissively" means in a meek, humble and obedient manner (yielding to others). Its antonym is "Proudly", meaning with dignity, self-respect and confidence. (विनम्रता/दब्बूपन से का विलोम — गर्व से)

◦ Example: The soldier stood proudly, not submissively, before the crowd.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Silently" (without noise), Option 2 "Civilly" (politely) and Option 3 "Magically" (as if by magic) are not opposites of submissively.

NOTE

• Synonyms of submissive: meek, obedient, yielding, docile, humble. Antonyms: proud, assertive, defiant, rebellious, dominant.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Shebna decided to take a break in social media, but she found it difficult to disconnect completely.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. a break from social media.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct collocation is "a break from (something)", meaning a period of rest or withdrawal away from it. So it should be "a break from social media".

◦ Correct: Shebna decided to take a break from social media ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "a break of", "a break up" and "a break down" are not the right prepositional phrases here.

• Note: "breakup" (end of a relationship) and "breakdown" (a failure/collapse) are different nouns with different meanings.

NOTE

• Preposition collocations: "take a break from work/study", "a break in the weather" (a pause), "break up with someone" (end a relationship).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Education is fundamental for achieving full human potential, developing an equitable and (1)__________ society, and promoting national development. Providing universal (2)__________ quality education is the key to India's continued ascent, and leadership on the global stage in terms of economic growth, social justice and equality, scientific advancement, national integration, and cultural preservation. Universal high-quality education is the best way (3)__________ for developing and maximising our country's rich talents and resources for the good (4)__________ the individual, the society, the country and the world. India (5)___________ the highest population of young people in the world over the next decade, and our ability to provide high-quality educational opportunities to them will determine the future of our country.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. just.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs an adjective parallel to "equitable" to describe "society". "Just" (fair, based on justice) fits perfectly — "an equitable and just society". (न्यायपूर्ण / निष्पक्ष)

◦ Correct: ... developing an equitable and just society ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "much", Option 3 "such" and Option 4 "more" are not adjectives that can describe "society" in parallel with "equitable"; they are determiners/quantifiers and do not fit grammatically.

NOTE

• "Equitable" (fair and impartial) and "just" (right and fair) are close in meaning, used together to stress fairness. Both are adjectives modifying "society".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Education is fundamental for achieving full human potential, developing an equitable and (1)__________ society, and promoting national development. Providing universal (2)__________ quality education is the key to India's continued ascent, and leadership on the global stage in terms of economic growth, social justice and equality, scientific advancement, national integration, and cultural preservation. Universal high-quality education is the best way (3)__________ for developing and maximising our country's rich talents and resources for the good (4)__________ the individual, the society, the country and the world. India (5)___________ the highest population of young people in the world over the next decade, and our ability to provide high-quality educational opportunities to them will determine the future of our country.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. access to.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct collocation is "access to (something)", meaning the opportunity or right to use/reach it. So it is "universal access to quality education".

◦ Correct: Providing universal access to quality education is the key ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "access at", "access from" and "access for" are incorrect prepositional combinations. The noun/verb "access" is always followed by "to".

NOTE

• Fixed collocation: "access to information / education / the internet". Example: "Everyone should have access to clean water."

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Education is fundamental for achieving full human potential, developing an equitable and (1)__________ society, and promoting national development. Providing universal (2)__________ quality education is the key to India's continued ascent, and leadership on the global stage in terms of economic growth, social justice and equality, scientific advancement, national integration, and cultural preservation. Universal high-quality education is the best way (3)__________ for developing and maximising our country's rich talents and resources for the good (4)__________ the individual, the society, the country and the world. India (5)___________ the highest population of young people in the world over the next decade, and our ability to provide high-quality educational opportunities to them will determine the future of our country.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. forward.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "the best way forward" is a common expression meaning the best course of action / the best method to make progress. It fits perfectly here. (आगे बढ़ने का सर्वोत्तम रास्ता)

◦ Correct: Universal high-quality education is the best way forward for developing and maximising our country's rich talents ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "outcome", 2 "output" and 3 "result" are nouns and would not fit the fixed phrase "the best way ___ for developing"; only "forward" makes it idiomatic.

NOTE

• "Way forward" = a plan or method for making progress. Example: "Dialogue is the only way forward in this dispute."

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Education is fundamental for achieving full human potential, developing an equitable and (1)__________ society, and promoting national development. Providing universal (2)__________ quality education is the key to India's continued ascent, and leadership on the global stage in terms of economic growth, social justice and equality, scientific advancement, national integration, and cultural preservation. Universal high-quality education is the best way (3)__________ for developing and maximising our country's rich talents and resources for the good (4)__________ the individual, the society, the country and the world. India (5)___________ the highest population of young people in the world over the next decade, and our ability to provide high-quality educational opportunities to them will determine the future of our country.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. of.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct phrase is "for the good of (someone/something)", meaning for the benefit of. So it is "for the good of the individual, the society, the country and the world".

◦ Correct: ... for the good of the individual, the society, the country and the world.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "the good from", "the good at" and "the good for" are not the correct prepositional phrase. The set expression is "for the good of".

NOTE

• "For the good of" = for the benefit/welfare of. Example: "The new law was passed for the good of the people."

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Education is fundamental for achieving full human potential, developing an equitable and (1)__________ society, and promoting national development. Providing universal (2)__________ quality education is the key to India's continued ascent, and leadership on the global stage in terms of economic growth, social justice and equality, scientific advancement, national integration, and cultural preservation. Universal high-quality education is the best way (3)__________ for developing and maximising our country's rich talents and resources for the good (4)__________ the individual, the society, the country and the world. India (5)___________ the highest population of young people in the world over the next decade, and our ability to provide high-quality educational opportunities to them will determine the future of our country.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. will have.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage refers to the future ("over the next decade"), so the simple future tense "will have" is correct. India will have the highest population of young people.

◦ Correct: India will have the highest population of young people in the world over the next decade ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "were having" is past continuous (wrong tense).

• Option 3 "might had" is grammatically incorrect (a modal is never followed by "had"; it should be "might have").

• Option 4 "can has" is grammatically wrong ("can" is always followed by the base form — "can have").

NOTE

• After a modal verb (will, can, might, may), always use the base form: "will have", "can have", "might have". "Over the next decade" signals the future tense.
